sourceBasis: Primary: NQR qualification file 'Analyst Security Operations Centre', IT-ITeS Sector Skills Council NASSCOM, NSQF level 5, NQR code QG-05-IT-01540-2023-V1.1-NASSCOM (QP SSC/Q0909, version 3; NSQC approval 25 Nov 2021), NOS SSC/N0906 and SSC/N0907, https://www.nqr.gov.in/qualification/file/SSC%20Q0909_Analyst%20Security%20Operations%20Centre_V3.pdf. Cross-checked: NQR OEM file 'Cybersecurity Analysis-IBM' (NG-05-IT-02239-2024-V1-NASSCOM); NIST NICE Framework work role Defensive Cybersecurity (PD-WRL-001); ONE job-role catalogue row C01. Levels, targets and evidence types are the agent's proposal for subject-expert review.

skills.name: Networking fundamentals for security monitoring
skills.description: TCP/IP, UDP, DNS, DHCP, HTTP and common ports; how traffic between hosts looks in logs and captures.
skills.basis: Q0909 Evidence of Level: 'Relevant networking concepts, devices, and terminology'; Tools annexure lists network protocols TCP/IP, UDP, DNS, DHCP, IPSEC, HTTP. Catalogue C01 core skill area 'Networking'.
skills.expertCheck: Check the protocol list is the right depth for L1 (IPSEC may be beyond entry level) and whether subnetting belongs here or in a separate skill.

skills.name: Windows and Linux log sources
skills.description: Where operating systems and applications record security-relevant events (for example Windows event logs, Linux system and authentication logs) and how to collect them.
skills.basis: SSC/N0906 PC8 'collect logs from all types of ICT systems devices and applications as required by the organisation'. Catalogue C01 core skill area 'Linux and Windows logs'.
skills.expertCheck: Check that naming Windows and Linux (and not macOS, network devices or cloud logs) is the right L1 scope; the qualification says 'all types of ICT systems'.

skills.name: Security fundamentals and common attacks
skills.description: Core security concepts, defence in depth, and the common vulnerability and attack types an analyst must recognise.
skills.basis: Q0909 Evidence of Level: 'Basic cyber security concepts', 'Knowledge of defence-in-depth principles'; SSC/N0907 PC15 'identify and categorize types of vulnerabilities and associated attacks'.
skills.expertCheck: Check the boundary with soc-vulnerability-basics so the two do not measure the same thing twice.

skills.name: Security monitoring with a SIEM
skills.description: Monitoring traffic and logs with security tools, collecting alert data through a SIEM, and spotting trends and patterns.
skills.basis: SSC/N0906 PC2, PC3 (monitor traffic and logs to detect threats), PC9 (collect data on alerts through SIEM), PC11 (identify trends and patterns using SIEM); N0907 PC24 (integrate assets with the SIEM). Tools annexure names SIEM tools.
skills.expertCheck: Check that the skill is assessable tool-neutrally (the qualification names several commercial SIEMs); ONE should not require a specific vendor.

skills.name: Alert triage and prioritisation
skills.description: Receiving alerts, working out their likely cause, separating real incidents from benign activity, and prioritising by potential impact.
skills.basis: SSC/N0907 PC1 (receive and analyse alarms and alerts, determine possible causes), PC6 (distinguish incidents from benign activities), PC10 (incident triage: scope, urgency, potential impact); SSC/N0906 PC15 (categorise priority of risks by potential impact). NICE PD-WRL-001 describes analysing data from defence tools to mitigate threats. Catalogue C01 'SIEM alert triage'.
skills.expertCheck: Check that triage is the right single skill or should split into 'identify false positives' and 'prioritise'; check whether scenario questions can evidence it before labs exist.

skills.name: Log analysis and event correlation
skills.description: Reading logs from several sources, correlating events, and drawing a conclusion about what happened and how serious it is.
skills.basis: SSC/N0906 PC13 (event correlation for situational awareness), PC14 (analysis of logs for identifying risks); SSC/N0907 PC2 (incorporate data from multiple tools), PC9 (analyse log files from a variety of sources), PC11 and PC12 (correlate data; correlate events using a SIEM).
skills.expertCheck: Check overlap with soc-security-monitoring-siem; the qualification spreads correlation across both NOS.

skills.name: Network traffic and packet analysis
skills.description: Characterising network traffic, using packet analysis to validate intrusion-detection alerts, and recognising denial-of-service patterns.
skills.basis: SSC/N0906 PC10 (characterise and analyse network traffic for anomalous activity); SSC/N0907 PC3 (validate IDS/IPS alerts using packet analysis tools), PC4 (deep packet analysis for DDoS/DoS vectors). Tools annexure names traffic analysis tools such as Wireshark.
skills.expertCheck: Check whether deep packet analysis is expected at L1 on entry or learned on the job; this is why it is proposed as IMPORTANT, not ESSENTIAL.

skills.name: Incident response process and escalation
skills.description: The incident-handling lifecycle as an L1 analyst lives it: scoping, preserving evidence, recommending actions, escalating what cannot be resolved, and closing incidents by procedure.
skills.basis: Q0909 Evidence of Level: 'Knowledge of incident response and handling methodologies'; SSC/N0907 PC5, PC7, PC13 (preserve evidence), PC16, PC17 (course of action, recommendations), PC20, PC21 (escalate; close incidents by procedure); SSC/N0906 PC20, PC26 (seek specialist help; use the escalation matrix). Catalogue C01 'incident response'.
skills.expertCheck: Check that an L1 is expected to recommend responses (PC17) and not only escalate; employer practice may differ.

skills.name: Mapping activity to MITRE ATT&CK
skills.description: Describing observed adversary behaviour in ATT&CK tactics and techniques so that findings are consistent and comparable.
skills.basis: Catalogue C01 core skill area 'MITRE ATT&CK'; Q0909 Tools annexure lists MITRE ATT&CK among 'Security Methodologies and Vulnerability Frameworks'; SSC/N0907 PC8 (determine exploitation methods and effects).
skills.expertCheck: The qualification lists ATT&CK as a tool rather than a performance criterion. Check whether it is expected of an L1 on entry.

skills.name: Ticketing, documentation and shift handover
skills.description: Recording and categorising tickets accurately, assigning them, documenting monitoring and incident work in the standard format, and giving and receiving shift handover.
skills.basis: SSC/N0906 PC16 to PC19 (record, raise, assign and prioritise tickets), PC21 (report results using standard documentation), PC22, PC23 (24/7 shift schedule; shift handover), PC25 (maintain a knowledge base); SSC/N0907 PC22, PC23 (report incident management; track incidents to resolution). Catalogue C01 'reporting'.
skills.expertCheck: Check the boundary with the existing professional-communication topic, which covers written handover in general terms.

skills.name: Using external threat information
skills.description: Following external sources such as CERT advisories and vendor bulletins, and using them during an investigation.
skills.basis: SSC/N0906 PC4 (monitor external data sources, e.g. CND vendor sites, Computer Emergency Response Teams, SANS, Security Focus); SSC/N0907 PC19 (use external information sources for incident investigation).
skills.expertCheck: Check whether CERT-In advisories should be named explicitly for Indian employers; the qualification names sources generically.

skills.name: Vulnerability scanning basics
skills.description: What a vulnerability scan does, how to read its findings, and how vulnerabilities relate to the alerts an analyst sees.
skills.basis: Q0909 Evidence of Level: 'how to conduct vulnerability scans and recognizing vulnerabilities in security systems', 'the security vulnerabilities associated with remote access technologies'.
skills.expertCheck: Check whether this belongs to C01 at all or mainly to C02 (VAPT associate); proposed as HELPFUL for that reason.

skills.name: Security policy, standards and legal compliance basics
skills.description: Awareness of the frameworks and standards SOC work operates under (for example NIST, ISO/IEC 27001, ITIL) and of complying with relevant legislation and organisational policy.
skills.basis: SSC/N0906 PC24 (comply with relevant legislation, standards, policies and procedures); Q0909 Evidence of Level: 'frameworks and management system standards like NIST, ITIL, ISO IEC 20000, ISO 27001'.
skills.expertCheck: Check whether Indian legislation (IT Act 2000, CERT-In reporting directions, DPDP Act 2023) should be named; the qualification does not name any.

requirements.rationale: Triage is the core of the L1 job: most of NOS SSC/N0907 is receiving alerts, separating real incidents from benign activity and judging urgency.
requirements.basis: SSC/N0907 PC1, PC6, PC10; SSC/N0906 PC15.
requirements.expertCheck: Target 0.70 mirrors the qualification's 70% minimum aggregate pass; a pass mark is not a mastery ratio, so confirm or change it.

requirements.rationale: Both mandatory NOS require analysing logs from several sources and correlating events before deciding whether something is a threat.
requirements.basis: SSC/N0906 PC13, PC14; SSC/N0907 PC2, PC9, PC11, PC12.
requirements.expertCheck: Confirm the level and the 0.70 target.

requirements.rationale: NOS SSC/N0906 is monitoring and logging events; alert data reaches an L1 analyst through a SIEM.
requirements.basis: SSC/N0906 PC2, PC3, PC9, PC11; SSC/N0907 PC24.
requirements.expertCheck: Confirm the level; confirm it can be evidenced without a specific vendor's SIEM.

requirements.rationale: An analyst cannot read an alert without knowing which system wrote the log behind it; the catalogue names Linux and Windows logs for this role.
requirements.basis: SSC/N0906 PC8; catalogue C01 core skill areas.
requirements.expertCheck: 0.65 is set a little below the analysis skills that build on it; confirm.

requirements.rationale: Networking concepts are named in the qualification's level justification and underpin traffic analysis, monitoring and triage.
requirements.basis: Q0909 Evidence of Level; Tools annexure (network protocols); catalogue C01.
requirements.expertCheck: Confirm ESSENTIAL rather than a prerequisite assumed from the degree (the qualification's entry requirement is UG or diploma study in engineering or science).

requirements.rationale: An L1 analyst must preserve evidence, recommend actions and escalate what they cannot resolve, following the incident procedure.
requirements.basis: SSC/N0907 PC5, PC7, PC13, PC16, PC17, PC20, PC21; SSC/N0906 PC20, PC26; Q0909 Evidence of Level.
requirements.expertCheck: Confirm the level and whether 0.65 is right for a process skill mostly learned on the job.

requirements.rationale: Ticketing, standard documentation and shift handover run through a large share of NOS SSC/N0906's performance criteria.
requirements.basis: SSC/N0906 PC16 to PC19, PC21 to PC23, PC25; SSC/N0907 PC22, PC23.
requirements.expertCheck: Confirm ESSENTIAL; check overlap with professional-communication.

requirements.rationale: Basic security concepts and recognising common attack and vulnerability types are the knowledge every other skill here relies on.
requirements.basis: Q0909 Evidence of Level; SSC/N0907 PC15.

requirements.rationale: Validating intrusion-detection alerts against traffic is in the qualification, but deep packet analysis is proposed as important rather than essential for a first SOC job.
requirements.expertCheck: The level is our judgement; the qualification does not grade criteria by importance.

requirements.rationale: The catalogue names MITRE ATT&CK for this role and the qualification lists it among the frameworks used; describing activity consistently makes escalations useful.
requirements.basis: Catalogue C01; Q0909 Tools annexure; SSC/N0907 PC8.
requirements.expertCheck: Confirm whether ATT&CK is expected on entry.

requirements.rationale: Using external advisories is in both NOS but is a smaller part of the L1 job than triage and analysis.
Named in the qualification's level justification, but vulnerability assessment is the main work of a different catalogue role (C02).
requirements.expertCheck: Confirm it belongs in C01 at all.

requirements.rationale: An analyst works within security standards and must comply with legislation and policy, but is not the person who writes or audits them.
requirements.basis: SSC/N0906 PC24; Q0909 Evidence of Level.
requirements.expertCheck: Confirm the level; decide whether Indian legislation should be named in the skill.

requirements.rationale: Incident handover and escalation notes are read by people acting on them under pressure.

requirements.expertCheck: Keep, change or remove: this requirement predates the qualification alignment.
